statement: Whenever find_intersection_values(nums1, nums2) returns a result r, len(r) = 2, r[0] is the cardinality of the set of indices i with 0 <= i < len(nums1) for which there exists j with 0 <= j < len(nums2) and nums2[j] = nums1[i], and r[1] is the cardinality of the set of indices j with 0 <= j < len(nums2) for which there exists i with 0 <= i < len(nums1) and nums1[i] = nums2[j].
preconditions: len(nums1) >= 1, len(nums2) >= 1, len(nums1) <= 100, len(nums2) <= 100, for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums1) we have 1 <= nums1[i] <= 100, and for every j with 0 <= j < len(nums2) we have 1 <= nums2[j] <= 100.

statement: Whenever find_intersection_values(nums1, nums2) returns a result r, for every integer v let c1(v) be the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(nums1) and nums1[i] = v, and let c2(v) be the number of indices j with 0 <= j < len(nums2) and nums2[j] = v. Then r[0] = (sum over all integers v of c1(v) * (1 if c2(v) > 0 else 0)) and r[1] = (sum over all integers v of c2(v) * (1 if c1(v) > 0 else 0)).
preconditions: len(nums1) >= 1, len(nums2) >= 1, len(nums1) <= 100, len(nums2) <= 100, for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums1) we have 1 <= nums1[i] <= 100, and for every j with 0 <= j < len(nums2) we have 1 <= nums2[j] <= 100.
